soundness_flags.label: Theorem 1 (star-source iff), and consequently Theorem 2 and Proposition 1
soundness_flags.one_line: The defined class P_+(mathfrak G,J) ranges over all completions h, while identifiability is claimed from S_J alone and Psi depends on h; define the fixed-h fiber P_{+,h} (or make revealed h part of the available source) before asserting completion-specific identification.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The published paper states that observational positivity is necessary for its repaired gID formulation and that its new algorithm is sound and complete by decomposition into classical-identifiability subproblems.
The paper studies arbitrary observational and experimental source collections, gives hedgelet/thicket non-gID machinery, and states a sound and complete gID procedure.
The paper seeks the highest-plausibility identifiable subgraph under probabilistic edge uncertainty and states NP-hardness of edge-ID.
The paper proves minimum-cost causal intervention design NP-complete, relates it to hitting sets, and treats fixed known causal graphs.
The paper gives reformulations for fixed-graph proxy experiment design and separately studies valid-adjustment-set design; it describes the earlier fixed-graph optimum-design problem as NP-complete.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Theorem 1.3 and Separating by Forbidden Pairs section
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The primary article states that Separating by Forbidden Pairs is Sigma_2^P-complete even on acyclic graphs.
The article proves Sigma_2^P-completeness for a broad family of minimum-cardinality interdiction/blocking problems through an abstract framework.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Introduce an explicitly completion-indexed class P_{+,h}(mathfrak G,J), state that h is revealed metadata available with S_J, and rewrite the iff, functional, and certificates uniformly over that fiber.

Promote the compiler audit into a standalone reduction lemma that states the exact encoding of an existential proxy choice, a universal switch assignment, selector isolation, and the auxiliary-cut rounding map.
